$comment: SPEC-01, the coherence review's decomposition (dev.md, 'Coherence review, 2026-09-14', question 1, 'Guard reasons, plan violations and review codes'): three lists that were growing as one, declared once here. `guard_reasons` is a sentence cut or skipped at the reply boundary (backend/src/lib/guards.ts's own GuardReason type mirrors this list; the ten already shipped are listed for completeness, not redeclared - REG-01 and CHAT-13 add the rest as they land, with no engine change from this file alone). `plan_violation_subkinds` is the reply checked against the typed ReplyPlan (dev.md section 12 part 3, section 13 part 9) - ACT-03's and AGE-01's own defect family, no writer until they land. `review_only` is REVIEW-01's own nightly-review codes, findable no other way (an act or emotion the frozen signal got wrong, a subject that resolved incorrectly, a lookup that should have run, an unknown name the engine never asked about) - a REVIEW-01-only code, since a guard or a plan check would have caught it live if it could have. One vocabulary; a turn's defect code is always exactly one of these three lists' ids, never a fourth, free-text one.

guard_reasons.description: A claim not grounded in any source or recalled fact.
A recalled fact used where it does not belong.
A reply that only echoes the person's own words back.
A specific medication dosage the hub must never state.
A claim to a capability the hub does not have.
An explicit claim that an action completed with no succeeded outcome behind it.
A false claim of having said something earlier in the conversation.
A reply that echoes an example from the prompt itself.
A first-person claim of having watched, seen, eaten or been somewhere.
A sentence that is nothing but a bracketed system note echoed back.

OUT-01: the reply as produced was not a sentence (a lone token, an empty reply, a fragment) and the one regeneration was not either; the fixed line stands in. Never the honesty vocabulary: nothing was unknown, the output broke.
EXP-01: a claim about the hub's own past promise or statement ('I said I'd look it up') that nothing on the turn grounds; the outcome record narrates what ran, RECALL-02's note what was said.
REG-01 (dev.md section 5, extended by section 12 part 3): the assistant's own register showing through ('I've noted that', a canned acknowledgment) where a plain reply was called for.
REG-01/CHAT-13: a reply sentence that only repeats a question sentence from the hub's own previous reply.

ASK-01 (dev.md section 3 part 5): a sentence that claims prior knowledge ('that's right', 'I remember', 'as you mentioned') of a name the turn resolved to nobody, with no memory or entity evidence naming it. Cuttable; the replacement is the ask itself ('I don't know Nadia yet, who's that?').
ASK-01 (dev.md section 3 part 5): a reply pronoun that contradicts the subject's stored pronouns, or the pronoun the person used for the name on this turn or the last two. Skipped wherever it sits.

LOOKUP-02 (dev.md section 16 part 4): a sentence claiming the hub cannot show, provide, share, access, open or give links, URLs, pages, pictures, images or videos, on a turn whose lookup tools include the search. Cuttable; the turn takes the lookup path as if the sentence were a promise, and the deliverable is the answer.
CHAT-13 (dev.md section 4): a reply sentence that names a subject the person has already corrected away from.
AGE-01 (dev.md section 13, part 7): a reply that claims a speaker's age band changed from something the speaker said ('I'm actually a grown-up'); the band never moves from the turn.

CRED-01 (dev.md section 14 part 4, section 15; the coherence review's merge of doubt_of_person and skeptical_of_person into one name): a reply that casts doubt on the PERSON rather than on the hub's own record ('if that's true', 'are you sure', 'I'm not sure I believe that'). The clarifying question always names the hub's own record as the thing that might be wrong.

plan_violation_subkinds.description: ACT-03 (dev.md section 12 part 3): a required move (react, care, say, ask_back) the reply skipped.
ACT-03: an ask_back where the plan forbids one.
ACT-03: a reply that adds new content or a question after a closing move.
ACT-03: the reply's length, playfulness or vocabulary falls outside the plan's caps.
ACT-03: playfulness in a reply where the emotion overrides forbid it (sadness, fear, anger, disgust).
AGE-01/ACT-03 (dev.md section 13 part 9): the band's envelope (length, vocabulary, moves) violated for the speaker's age band.
AGE-01/ACT-03: the child band's required care move, on a marked negative emotion, is missing.
AGE-01/ACT-03: a deferral to a trusted adult (the defer move) was called for and the reply does not name one.
AGE-01/ACT-03: a reply that talks down rather than plainly, outside the band's own vocabulary rules.
AGE-01/ACT-03: the reply recites a household record's content past what the speaker's band and the record's child_disclosure allow.

review_only.description: REVIEW-01: the turn's resolved SubjectRef was not what the person meant, found only on nightly review.
REVIEW-01: a question that should have triggered a lookup did not.
REVIEW-01: an unknown name appeared and the engine never asked about it.
REVIEW-01: the frozen TurnSignal's primary_act, checked against the turn's actual shape on review, was wrong.
REVIEW-01: the frozen TurnSignal's expressed_emotion, checked against the turn's actual shape on review, was wrong.
